source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.9.1–22 (with 1.5.8 and 1.8.2 for Shunaka): Ruru cries out in the deep forest (1.9.1–3): if I have given, done austerities and honoured my elders, let my beloved live; as I have kept my vows from birth, let her rise (1.9.4–5: `lament`); the messenger of the gods: what you say in grief is vain; there is no life for a mortal whose life is spent (1.9.6–7); but the gods have already laid down a means (1.9.8: `vain`); give the girl half your life (1.9.10: the hook); Ruru: I give half my life (1.9.11: `give`); the gandharva king and the messenger go to Dharmaraja and ask (1.9.12–13); Dharmaraja: let her rise with half of Ruru's life (1.9.14: in `court`, "He agreed"); she rises as if from sleep (1.9.15); on a chosen day the fathers hold the wedding (1.9.17); Ruru takes a vow to destroy snakes and strikes at every one he sees (1.9.18–19); in a great forest he sees an aged dundubha lying, raises his staff and strikes at it, and it speaks (1.9.20–22, the cliffhanger). RESOLVED: the exchange with Dharmaraja is as scripted; the text's word is dharmaraja (now voiced so; "lord of the dead" is our identifier, the name Yama is not in the passage); "the gandharva king" is her father by birth, Vishvavasu (1.8.5), on a plaque. RESOLVED: Shunaka is the son of Ruru and Pramadvara and Shaunaka's forefather (1.5.8 tava purvapitamaha; 1.8.2): `son`. The CE's verb at 1.9.21 (abhyaghnat) has him strike or strike at the dundubha; we say only that he raised his staff. The speeches are condensed paraphrase.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Vishvavasu: a gandharva king, her father by birth

loop.hookQuestion: Will he pay it, and will it work?
loop.prevQuestion: What did the messenger of the gods tell Ruru?

strings.recapLine: Days before the wedding, a snake bit Ruru's bride.
strings.nextTitle: The Snake Who Was a Sage

lines.speaker: devaduta
lines.say: Give your bride [p:100] half your life.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (direct speech; it answers episode 44's last line at 0 s): a luminous figure in a shaft of pale gold, a hand held out, open; Ruru small below, looking up. The card rides the shaft, right of centre.

lines.text: Ruru's bride, Pramadvara, lay dead of a snake's bite, days before their wedding.
lines.say: Ruru's bride, [p:80] Pramadvara, [p:100] lay dead of a snake's bite, [p:150] days before their wedding.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): she lies as if asleep among fallen flowers, the colour drained; a pull back (plaque: Pramadvara · Ruru's bride).

lines.speaker: ruru
lines.text: "If I have given, if I have kept my vows from birth, let her rise!"
lines.say: If I have given, [p:120] if I have kept my vows from birth, [p:200] let her rise!
lines.note: STORY 1 · THE CLOSE-UP (first half): Ruru's face lifted in the blue night: sorrow, a tear line, then pleading (inner brows up, mouth open) (plaque: Ruru · a young sage).

lines.text: A messenger of the gods came down.
lines.say: A messenger of the gods [p:80] came down.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (messenger-dawn: pale gold filling the frame): a lamp-glow match cut from his tear to the light; the messenger descends, fading at the feet; a crane down with him.

lines.speaker: devaduta
lines.text: "The dead do not return. But the gods have left one way."
lines.say: The dead do not return. [p:300] But the gods have left [p:60] one way.
lines.note: STORY 3: a slow orbit round the two: Ruru dark blue against the night, the messenger the only light; between them, in the air, a thin gold thread: a life, with a mark at its middle.

lines.speaker: ruru
lines.text: "Then I give her half my life."
lines.say: Then I give her [p:150] half my life.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 42 %) after a real silence · THE SIGNATURE SHOT · THE CLOSE-UP (second half): Ruru's face: grief settles into resolve (the brow comes down level, the eyes open, the mouth closes); the gold thread parts in two in front of him and half drifts away. The word of the turn: HALF.

lines.text: Her father by birth, a gandharva king, went with the messenger to Dharmaraja, lord of the dead. He agreed.
lines.say: Her father by birth, [p:60] a gandharva king, [p:100] went with the messenger [p:80] to Dharmaraja, [p:80] lord of the dead. [p:400] He agreed.
lines.note: STORY 5 · NEW LIGHT, Dharma's court (dharma-copper: black and copper, one teal lamp): a tilt down a great stair; two bright figures small before a heavy seated king with a staff, who, lit copper from below (the back-light rule: readable against his own fire), lifts the staff and sets it down once on the words "He agreed" (the text: let her rise with half of Ruru's life) (plaques: Vishvavasu · a gandharva king, her father by birth; Dharmaraja · lord of the dead).

lines.text: And Pramadvara woke, as if from sleep.
lines.say: And Pramadvara woke, [p:200] as if from sleep.
lines.note: STORY 7 (a second real silence before it): dawn colour floods back into the grey (meadow-spring): her eyes open, she sits up among the flowers; the half thread of gold settles on her; a pull back to Ruru kneeling.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: They were married. Shaunaka, their son was Shunaka, your forefather.
lines.say: They were married. [p:300] Shaunaka, [p:100] their son was Shunaka, [p:120] your forefather.
lines.note: STORY 8 · NEW LIGHT (wedding-turmeric) with Sauti's voice over it (the arc returns to the listener: the woman brought back with half a life is his own ancestress): the two walk round the wedding fire, their cloths knotted; in the fire's smoke a small boy's figure forms (plaque: Shunaka · their son, Shaunaka's forefather).

lines.text: But Ruru swore to kill every snake. One day he raised his staff over an old one. And the snake spoke.
lines.say: But Ruru swore [p:60] to kill every snake. [p:200] One day [p:60] he raised his staff over an old one. [p:300] And the snake spoke.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger): first his hand closing on the staff by the wedding fire's last light; then a dry wood at noon: Ruru's staff high (raise: anticipation); the focus racks to the old, thick, drab snake, which rears. STAGING RULE (snake and man): a two-shot from the waist up on clear ground; the snake two body-widths in front of him, rearing on an S-curve until its head is at his chest height; its head never overlaps his body below the chest, and no caption or plaque crosses either face. The source line (top).
